script: This curve passes through every single point. That's the problem.
Twenty noisy points. Let's fit a polynomial, starting with a straight line.
Raise the degree, and the curve bends to follow the points. The error on these twenty points keeps falling.
At degree 19, it passes through all twenty. Error: zero.
Now test it on five thousand new points from the same source. The error jumps to 84.
Too simple misses the shape. Too flexible memorizes the noise. Degrees 3 to 7 all do about the same: zero point two nine.
Fix one: more data. With two hundred points, degree 19 behaves: zero point two six on new points.
Fix two: a small penalty on big coefficients. Back to twenty points, degree 19: zero point three one.
A perfect score on your own data isn't the goal. The error on new data is.
